tracks.name: Inzpire
tracks.summary: The API track. You write the code and host the endpoints: SMS, USSD, CaaS, Subscription, OTP and LBS. This skill is about Inzpire.

tracks.name: Xpand
tracks.summary: The no-code track. Contact, Vote, Alert and Scheduled Messages applications created and managed through the platform without writing code.

operators.name: Mobitel
operators.note: The operator selected when provisioning an application. The mSpace provisioning guide describes it as the prime provider of the APIs.

baseUrls.configuration: Configure one URL per provisioned service (MSPACE_SMS_SEND_URL, MSPACE_USSD_SEND_URL, …). An unset endpoint means that API is not enabled on the application, and the client should refuse to call it rather than fail with E1309 at the platform. See templates/.env.example.

auth.note: Every outbound request carries applicationId and password in the JSON body. There are no headers, tokens or signatures. For the CaaS services the password is the API key sent to the registered email address on application approval.

rules: Always tel:-prefixed, no + and no spaces. The documented format is tel:94702725777.
May be a masked number when Mobile Number Masking is enabled on the application. Treat it as opaque.
tel:all sends to the subscribed base of the application (SMS send only).

responseEnvelope.criticalNote: mSpace returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Branch on statusCode, never on the HTTP status alone. S1000 is success — except on CaaS OTP generation, where the documented success code is P1003, and on Subscriber List, where S1001 means the request succeeded and matched nobody.

services.name: SMS Send
services.summary: Send an MT (Mobile Terminated) SMS to one or more terminals from your application.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on. If a version is specified in the request the same version is returned in the response; if it is not, the latest version is returned.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Content of the message to send. Messages over the limit are broken up by the platform before sending.

parameters.name: destinationAddresses
parameters.description: List of destination addresses, which should be telephone numbers (tel: for MSISDN), for example tel:94702725777. Always an array, even for one recipient. The value tel:all sends the message to the subscribed base of the application. tel may be a masked number depending on the type of application.

parameters.name: sourceAddress
parameters.description: Address of the source shown to the subscriber. Must be the default sender address or one of the send address aliases configured in provisioning, or the send fails with E1331.

parameters.name: deliveryStatusRequest
parameters.description: Indicates the need of a Delivery Status Report for the message. 0 = not required, 1 = required.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Encoding scheme used in the message: 0 = Text, 240 = Flash SMS, 245 = Binary. If not specified it is taken as Text. With Binary the message content is represented hex encoded.

parameters.name: binaryHeader
parameters.description: Hexadecimal. For advanced types of message where the binary header is sent from the application.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies a request within the platform.

responseFields.name: destinationResponses
responseFields.description: The list of responses for the full list of addresses, with one entry for each element in the address list of the request. A multi-recipient send can partially succeed, so branch on each entry's statusCode, not only the top-level one.

fields.name: address
fields.description: The tel:-prefixed recipient this entry reports on.

fields.name: messageId
fields.description: Message identifier for this recipient. Store it to match delivery reports.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: Outcome for this recipient alone.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Human-readable outcome for this recipient.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: Processed timestamp for this recipient.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 on success.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

rules: destinationAddresses is always an array, even for a single recipient.
Guard tel:all behind a deliberate, separately-authorised code path — it reaches the whole subscribed base.
sourceAddress must be the default sender address or a configured alias, or the send fails with E1331.
Only set deliveryStatusRequest to 1 if you actually consume the delivery report callback.
There is no top-level messageId: per-recipient identifiers live in destinationResponses.

services.name: USSD Send
services.summary: Send a USSD message (a screen) to a mobile phone from your application.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on. If a version is specified in the request the same version is returned in the response.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Content of the message sent by the application — the screen text the subscriber sees.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique number the USSD Gateway assigns to the application for the duration of the session. It is maintained in all the messages throughout a single session, so echo the one you were given rather than generating your own.

parameters.name: ussdOperation
parameters.description: The USSD operation. An application assigns mt-init when it initiates a session, mt-cont for any message that comes after an init, and mt-fin when the session ends in a final message. mo-init and mo-cont are assigned by the platform for messages originated by the subscriber.

parameters.name: destinationAddress
parameters.description: Destination address, which should be a telephone number (tel: for MSISDN). May be a masked number depending on the type of application.

parameters.name: encoding
parameters.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 440 = plain ASCII characters.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: requestId
responseFields.description: Uniquely identifies the request within the platform.

responseFields.name: timeStamp
responseFields.description: Processed timestamp.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. S1000 on success.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

sampleRequest.message:
1. Press One
2. Press two
3. Press three
4. Exit

rules: Echo the sessionId the platform gave you. Never generate one for a session the platform started.
mt-fin closes the session. Terminal screens must use it, or the session hangs until the network times it out.
encoding 440 is plain ASCII: no emoji, no Sinhala or Tamil script, no smart quotes.
Reply fast. Do the minimum inline and defer anything slow to an out-of-band job.

services.name: Subscription Register (opt-in)
services.summary: Opt a subscriber in to the application. The same endpoint handles unsubscription with action 0.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN of the subscriber, tel:-prefixed — for example tel:94716177301. May be a masked number depending on the type of application. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 1 = user subscription, 0 = user unsubscription.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Status of the subscription, for example REGISTERED or UNREGISTERED.

rules: Capture explicit consent before calling this, and record what the user agreed to, when, and through which channel.
Disclose the charging amount and frequency before subscribing — both are set per application in provisioning.
Registration may land in INITIAL or REG_PENDING rather than REGISTERED. Do not start delivering the service until the subscription is active.
Mirror subscription state in your own database rather than calling getStatus on every request.

services.name: Subscription Unregister (opt-out)
services.summary: Opt a subscriber out of the application. The same endpoint as register, with action 0.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN of the subscriber, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: 1 = user subscription, 0 = user unsubscription.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Status of the subscription, for example REGISTERED or UNREGISTERED.

rules: Unregister must be as easy to reach as register: an opt-out keyword over MO SMS, a USSD menu option, and an in-app control.
Honour an opt-out immediately, including cancelling messages you have already queued for that subscriber.
Never re-subscribe a subscriber who opted out without a fresh, separate opt-in.

services.name: Subscriber Status
services.summary: Return the subscription status of one subscriber.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Unique identification of the application within the platform.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password given when provisioning the application.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN of the subscriber, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Status of the subscription: INITIAL, REG_PENDING, TRIAL, REGISTERED, UNREGISTERED or TEMPORARY_BLOCKED.

rules: Use it for reconciliation — a nightly sweep, or when a subscriber disputes their state — not as a per-request gate.
There are six documented statuses, not two. Handle INITIAL, REG_PENDING, TRIAL and TEMPORARY_BLOCKED explicitly.

services.name: Query Base (subscriber base size)
services.summary: Return the number of subscribers currently registered to the application.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

responseFields.name: baseSize
responseFields.description: Number of registered users. Arrives as a string — coerce it before arithmetic.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

rules: Needs no subscriber and charges nothing, which makes it the safest call for proving credentials, provisioning and the egress IP.
baseSize is a string. Parse it before charting or comparing.
Poll it on a schedule into your own metrics store rather than per page load, and sanity-check it before any tel:all broadcast.

services.name: Subscriber Charging Info
services.summary: Return subscription status and last-charge details for up to ten subscribers in one request.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Unique identification of the application within the platform.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password given when provisioning the application.

parameters.name: subscriberIds
parameters.description: MSISDNs of the list of subscribers, for example ["tel:94712342345", "tel:94712678845"]. If the application accepts masked numbers, the masked numbers must be sent here. The list can contain a maximum of 10 MSISDNs per request.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: destinationResponses
responseFields.description: One entry per subscriber in the request. Which fields are populated depends on the subscription status, so read defensively.

fields.name: subscriberId
fields.description: MSISDN of the subscriber, masked if the application accepts masked numbers. Always present.

fields.name: subscriptionStatus
fields.description: INITIAL, REG_PENDING, TRIAL, REGISTERED, UNREGISTERED or TEMPORARY_BLOCKED.

fields.name: lastChargedDate
fields.description: The successful last charged date of the subscriber, in the format YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss. Omitted for a free application.

fields.name: lastChargedAmount
fields.description: The successful last charged amount for the subscriber with the currency code, for example 30.00 LKR. Sent as 0.00 LKR for a free application.

fields.name: numberType
fields.description: Denotes whether the subscriber is prepaid or postpaid.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: Success or error code for this subscriber.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Description of the status for this subscriber.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

rules: Maximum 10 MSISDNs per request. Batch larger sets by looping with your own rate limiting.
lastChargedDate and lastChargedAmount are absent for INITIAL, REG_PENDING and TRIAL subscribers — check before reading them.
Every entry carries its own statusCode. One subscriber failing does not fail the request.

services.name: Subscriber List
services.summary: Retrieve the subscriber list a page at a time, so you can catch up on subscription notifications you missed.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Unique identification of the application within the platform.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password given when provisioning the application.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version.

parameters.name: requestPage
parameters.description: The specific page number from a list of pages containing subscription notifications. Must be 1 or greater, or the request fails with E1106.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: Success or error code for each subscriber and for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description corresponding to the status code.

responseFields.name: nextPageNumber
responseFields.description: The next page number available. If there is no page available next, -1 is returned.

responseFields.name: moreDataAvailable
responseFields.description: Indicates whether there is more data available.

responseFields.name: subscribers
responseFields.description: Subscriber data for this page.

fields.name: subscriberId
fields.description: MSISDN of the subscriber, masked if the application accepts masked numbers.

fields.name: subscriptionStatus
fields.description: Status of the subscription, for example TRIAL, REGISTERED or TEMPORARY_BLOCKED.

fields.name: lastChargedDate
fields.description: The successful last charged date of the subscriber, in the format YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.

fields.name: lastChargedAmount
fields.description: The successful last charged amount for the subscriber with the currency code.

rules: S1001 (No Subscribers Found) is not a failure. The request worked and matched nobody — treat it as success.
Page until moreDataAvailable is false; nextPageNumber is -1 when there is no next page.
This endpoint has its own E11xx status-code family, not the E13xx one the other services use.
It is a catch-up mechanism for missed notifications, not a substitute for handling the Subscription Notification URL.

services.name: Subscriber Notification

parameters.name: timeStamp
parameters.description: The timestamp, in the format yyMMddHHmm: yy last two digits of the year (00-99), MM month (01-12), dd day (01-31), HH hour (00-23), mm minute (00-59).

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Authenticates the application-originated message against the credentials of the service provider. Encoded, single value.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN of the subscriber, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Frequency of notifications being sent.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Status of the subscription, for example UNREGISTERED or REGISTERED.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Description of the status for the entire request.

rules: This is the same field vocabulary the Subscription Notification URL uses. Provisioning configures that URL separately, under Subscription configuration.
Do not use it to reconstruct state you should be mirroring from the Subscription Notification URL.

services.name: OTP Request
services.summary: Request an OTP for a subscriber's MSISDN. mSpace generates and sends the OTP; the subscriber enters it in your application to activate a subscription.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: ID of the application.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password or API key given to uniquely identify the application.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: Mobile number of the end consumer, tel:-prefixed.

parameters.name: applicationHash
parameters.description: Hash string to determine which verification messages to send to your app.

parameters.name: applicationMetaData
parameters.description: Client details for the request: client (client type — web browser or mobile app), device (type or OS of device, e.g. iPhone 6, Galaxy S5, PC), os (OS or device version, e.g. Android 6, iOS 5, Windows 10) and appCode (your app identifier in the store, or the web link if you use a browser).

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. When the request is successful, statusCode is S1000.

responseFields.name: referenceNo
responseFields.description: Reference key that uniquely identifies the request. Keep it server-side and pass it to OTP Verify.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: The status detail for the entire request.

rules: Call it from a backend with a whitelisted IP, never from the browser or the mobile app.
Keep referenceNo server-side, in the session. Never send it to the client and never put it in a URL.
Rate-limit per number and per IP yourself. Without that the application is an SMS-bombing tool aimed at arbitrary numbers, at your expense.
Never log the OTP or the referenceNo.

services.name: OTP Verify
services.summary: Verify the OTP a subscriber entered. On success the mSpace subscription process is activated and the masked subscriberId is returned.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: ID of the application.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password or API key given to uniquely identify the application.

parameters.name: referenceNo
parameters.description: Reference number returned with the OTP Request API.

parameters.name: otp
parameters.description: The one time password to be used for MSISDN verification for the application.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the entire request. When the request is successful, statusCode is S1000.

responseFields.name: subscriptionStatus
responseFields.description: Subscription status of the user.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: The status detail for the entire request.

responseFields.name: subscriberId
responseFields.description: Masked mobile number of the end consumer. The application has to use this for any subsequent request sent to the platform.

rules: The subscriberId returned here is the masked identifier. Store it as the subscriber's identity for every later mSpace call.
E1851 (expired) and E1852 (maximum attempts reached) are the documented limits. mSpace does not publish the validity window or the attempt count, so enforce your own limits as well.
Never log the OTP.

services.name: CaaS OTP Generation (direct debit)
services.summary: Start a one-time charge on the subscriber's mobile account. mSpace generates and sends an OTP to the subscriber's MSISDN, which they must enter in your application to authorise the charge.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address on the platform upon application approval.

parameters.name: externalTrxId
parameters.description: The transaction ID generated by the application to map the request with the response. It is needed to provide information when there are inquiries related to a transaction. Only a single value per request. Persist it BEFORE calling — it is the idempotency key.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: The MSISDN of the subscriber to be charged, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: paymentInstrumentName
parameters.description: The name of the payment instrument. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Amount to be reserved for charging, sent as a string. Only a single value per request. Hold it as a decimal type in your own code.

parameters.name: currency
parameters.description: Currency unit of the amount. Only LKR is allowed. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: applicationHash
parameters.description: A unique hash value generated by the service provider application to ensure request integrity and authenticity, using a mutually agreed hashing algorithm (for example SHA-256) over agreed request parameters. Only a single value per request.

responseFields.name: timeStamp
responseFields.description: The time that the request was sent.

responseFields.name: externalTrxId
responseFields.description: Echo of the transaction ID you generated. Assert it matches what you sent.

responseFields.name: requestCorrelator
responseFields.description: The unique identifier used internally within the system to identify the transaction. Pass it as referenceNo to CaaS OTP Verification.

responseFields.name: internalTrxId
responseFields.description: The transaction ID generated by the service provider which can be used to track the transaction. Persist it — this is what support traces with.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status of the request. P1003 means the OTP was sent successfully; it is the success code for this call, not S1000.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: Detailed description explaining the status of the entire request.

rules: The success code is P1003, not S1000. Code that only accepts S1000 reports every successful charge request as a failure.
P1003 means the OTP was sent — nothing has been charged yet. The charge happens on CaaS OTP Verification and settles on the charging notification.
externalTrxId is your idempotency key. Generate it once, persist it BEFORE the call, and reuse the same value for any retry of that same logical charge.
Never retry a charge with a fresh externalTrxId. A timeout does not mean the charge did not happen.
Amount and currency come from server-side configuration or a server-side price lookup, never from client input.

services.name: CaaS OTP Verification
services.summary: Verify the OTP the subscriber entered. On successful verification the one-time charge is deducted from the subscriber's mobile account.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Identifies the application. A unique identifier generated while provisioning. Only a single value per request.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: The API key sent to your registered email address on the platform upon application approval.

parameters.name: referenceNo
parameters.description: The value returned for requestCorrelator in the response of the CaaS OTP generation request. It is the reference of the transaction.

parameters.name: otp
parameters.description: The OTP entered by the subscriber on the developer application.

parameters.name: sourceAddress
parameters.description: The MSISDN that requested the OTP, tel:-prefixed.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status of the request. S1000 means it was successfully processed.

responseFields.name: statusDescription
responseFields.description: Human-readable description of the outcome. Note the field is statusDescription here, not statusDetail.

responseFields.name: status
responseFields.description: true if the OTP was valid and charging proceeded; false otherwise.

rules: referenceNo is the requestCorrelator from the OTP generation response, not your externalTrxId.
The description field is statusDescription on this endpoint, not statusDetail. A shared response parser that only reads statusDetail loses the message.
Read both statusCode and status: the boolean is the plain answer to whether charging proceeded.
The final outcome still arrives on the charging notification. Reconcile against that, not against this response alone.
Never log the OTP or the referenceNo.

services.name: LBS Request Location
services.summary: Request the location of a subscriber. mSpace returns the location if the subscriber has granted permission.

parameters.name: applicationId
parameters.description: Application identification within the platform.

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: Password of the application.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: API version.

parameters.name: requesterId
parameters.description: MSISDN of the subscriber who is requesting the location updates, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application.

parameters.name: subscriberId
parameters.description: MSISDN of the subscriber whose location is needed, tel:-prefixed. May be a masked number depending on the type of application.

parameters.name: serviceType
parameters.description: Required MLP service type. Currently supports IMMEDIATE.

responseFields.name: version
responseFields.description: API version.

responseFields.name: messageID
responseFields.description: Message identifier that uniquely identifies the request within the platform. Note the capital D.

responseFields.name: latitude
responseFields.description: Latitude coordinate of the location of the subscriber. A string, and absent on failure.

responseFields.name: longitude
responseFields.description: Longitude coordinate of the location of the subscriber. A string, and absent on failure.

responseFields.name: subscriberState
responseFields.description: Power on/off state of the target subscriber's mobile phone. true = power on, false = power off.

responseFields.name: timestamp
responseFields.description: System date and time of the successful or failed transaction. Note the lower-case s.

responseFields.name: statusCode
responseFields.description: The status code for the request.

responseFields.name: statusDetail
responseFields.description: The status detail for the request.

rules: requesterId is mandatory and separate from subscriberId — the requester and the located subscriber are two different fields.
latitude and longitude are strings, and absent on failure. Check they exist before reading them.
One subscriber per request. Batch by looping with rate limiting, not by passing an array.
Obtain and record explicit, purpose-specific consent before locating anyone. Consent to receive SMS is not consent to be located.

callbacks.name: SMS Receive (MO)
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber sends an SMS to your short code with your keyword. The platform delivers it to the Message Receiving URL you configured.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID — verify it matches yours.

fields.name: sourceAddress
fields.description: Address of the source, tel:-prefixed. Masked if Mobile Number Masking is enabled.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Content of the message sent by the user, including the keyword.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies a request within the platform.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: Encoding scheme used in the message: 0 = Text, 240 = Flash SMS, 245 = Binary. With Binary the message content is hex encoded.

rules: Recognise opt-out keywords such as STOP, UNSUB and OFF, and honour them by calling Subscription Unregister.
Do not perform a destructive or chargeable action on the content of one MO SMS alone — it is unauthenticated beyond the source address.

callbacks.name: SMS Delivery Report
callbacks.summary: Fires when an MT SMS sent with deliveryStatusRequest 1 reaches a final state. Match it to the original send with messageId or requestId.

fields.name: destinationAddress
fields.description: Address of the subscriber, tel:-prefixed.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: The timestamp sent from the SMS, in the format yyMMddHHmm: yy last two digits of the year (00-99), MM month (01-12), dd day (01-31), HH hour (00-23), mm minute (00-59). The documented sample is 14 digits, so parse on length.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies a request within the platform. Ties the report back to the original send.

fields.name: deliveryStatus
fields.description: The delivery outcome the platform reports to the application.

rules: ACCEPTED is not DELIVERED — it means the network took the message, nothing more.
Reports can arrive out of order, late, more than once, or never. Store the latest status keyed by requestId and keep the handler idempotent.

callbacks.name: USSD Receive
callbacks.summary: Fires when a subscriber dials your service code or presses a key in an open session. The platform delivers the MO message to your Connection URL as a delivery request.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: applicationId
fields.description: Your application ID — verify it matches yours.

fields.name: message
fields.description: Content of the message sent by the user — what they dialled or typed.

fields.name: requestId
fields.description: Uniquely identifies a request within the platform.

fields.name: sessionId
fields.description: Unique number the USSD Gateway assigns to the application for the duration of the session. Echo it back on every screen you send.

fields.name: ussdOperation
fields.description: The USSD operation. Inbound it is mo-init when the subscriber starts a session, or mo-cont for a message that comes after an init.

fields.name: sourceAddress
fields.description: Address of the source, tel:-prefixed. Masked if Mobile Number Masking is enabled.

fields.name: vlrAddress
fields.description: VLR (Visitor Location Register) address of the sender.

fields.name: encoding
fields.description: Encoding scheme used in the message. 440 = plain ASCII characters.

rules: The response body is only an acknowledgement. The screen the subscriber sees comes from a separate POST /ussd/send.
Acknowledge immediately — USSD sessions time out in seconds — then build the next screen out of band.

callbacks.name: Charging Notification
callbacks.summary: Returned to your application upon a charging attempt, saying whether the charging succeeded. There is nothing to trigger: it arrives automatically once the transaction completes within the system.

fields.name: timeStamp
fields.description: The time at which the request was sent.

fields.name: version
fields.description: API version, numbered 1.0, 2.0 and so on.

fields.name: externalTrxId
fields.description: The transaction ID generated by the application to map the request with the response. This is the key to reconcile against your own ledger.

fields.name: internalTrxId
fields.description: The unique identifier used to track the request at the developer application end.

fields.name: referenceId
fields.description: The unique reference used to identify the transaction within the system.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: Currency unit of the amount. Only LKR is allowed.

fields.name: TotalAmount
fields.description: Amount deducted from the subscriber as the one time charge. Note the capital T.

fields.name: paidAmount
fields.description: The amount that is paid by the subscriber.

fields.name: balanceDue
fields.description: The amount that is due, if any; otherwise 0.

fields.name: statusCode
fields.description: The status of the charging attempt. S1000 means the request was successfully processed and the due amount was fully paid.

fields.name: statusDetail
fields.description: Detailed description explaining the status of the entire request.

samplePayload.statusDetail: Request was Successfully processed, Due amount fully paid.

rules: This is your reconciliation channel. Every charge your code left in an unknown state after a timeout gets settled here.
Match on externalTrxId — the key you generated and persisted before the OTP generation call.
Deduplicate on externalTrxId plus statusCode. A repeat notification for an already-charged transaction must not double-count revenue.
The amount field is TotalAmount with a capital T, and it sits alongside paidAmount and balanceDue. Read all three before deciding the charge is complete.

pending.action: Accepted, not complete. The outcome arrives later — on the charging notification, or after the subscriber acts. Do not treat it as a finished operation, and do not re-send the request.

configuration.action: Provisioning or credentials are wrong. Fix the application record — code changes will not help. Alert on these in production; the integration is down, not one request.

client.action: Your payload is wrong, or the user gave bad input. Fix the request or prompt the user.

user-state.action: The subscriber is not eligible right now. Communicate; do not retry in a loop.

transient.action: Platform-side. Exponential backoff with jitter, capped attempts, then dead-letter.

S1000.description: Process completed successfully. On Subscriber List it reads "Request Was Successfully Processed"; on SMS send, "Process completed successfully for all the available destination numbers".

S1001.fix: The request succeeded and matched nobody. Treat it as success and stop paging.

P1003.fix: This is the success code for CaaS OTP generation — nothing has been charged yet. Store requestCorrelator, collect the OTP from the subscriber, and call CaaS OTP Verification.

E1102.description: Service Provider Is Not In Active Status.

E1103.description: Request Parameters are Invalid. Refer the API documentation.

E1104.description: Application is Not in Active or Limited Production Status.

E1105.fix: Throttle your own request rate and retry with backoff.

E1106.description: Invalid Request Page. Page Number Should Be 1 Or Greater.

E1107.description: Request Is Invalid. Refer the API documentation for the mandatory fields and correct format of the request.

E1300.fix: Log the full response and escalate with the externalTrxId if it persists.

E1301.description: Requested ApplicationID is not allowed within the System for the operator.

E1302.description: Requested SP is not allowed within the System.

E1303.description: IP address, which the request originates from, is not listed within the allowed-host-address list.
E1303.fix: Add the calling server's egress IP to Allowed Host Address on the application record. Determine it from the server that makes the calls, not from a laptop.

E1308.description: Permanent charging error, for example insufficient balance.
E1308.fix: Tell the subscriber. Do not blind-retry.

E1309.description: Requested SMS service is not allowed for this application.
E1309.fix: The API was not provisioned for this application. Fix the application record; no payload change helps.

E1311.description: Mobile terminated SMS messages are not enabled. Check the NCS configuration in provisioning.

E1312.fix: Check the mandatory fields and the format of the request against the endpoint's parameter table.

E1313.description: Authentication failed. There is no active application with the given applicationId, or no active service provider, or the password in the request is invalid.
E1313.fix: Check MSPACE_APP_ID and MSPACE_PASSWORD, and that the application is active.

E1315.description: Cannot find the requested service, or it is not active. On the CaaS path this is reported as "NCS system unavailable".

E1317.description: The MSISDN in the request is invalid or not allowed.
E1317.fix: Validate the number. Do not retry.

E1318.description: Transaction limit per second has exceeded.
E1318.fix: Throttle requests so they stay under the transaction limit.

E1319.description: Transaction limit for today has exceeded.
E1319.fix: Try again tomorrow, or have the per-day transaction limit raised.

E1325.description: Format of the address is invalid. The expected format is tel:94702725777.
E1325.fix: A missing tel: prefix, or a + or a space that slipped in.

E1329.description: Charging amount too high. Check the NCS configuration.

E1330.description: Charging amount too low. Check the NCS configuration.

E1331.fix: Use the default sender address or one of the send address aliases configured on the application, or omit sourceAddress so the platform uses the default.

E1335.description: Advertisement message length is too long.

E1337.fix: The subscriber did not confirm. Prompt them again rather than retrying automatically.

E1341.description: Request failed. Errors occurred while sending the request for all the destinations.

E1342.description: The MSISDN is blacklisted and is not authorised to use this application.
E1342.fix: Check Blacklisted Numbers on the application record.

E1343.description: The MSISDN is not whitelisted. Only whitelisted numbers are allowed at this state.
E1343.fix: Add the test number under Whitelisted Numbers while the application is in Limited Production.

E1371.description: The application does not accept payments from the given payment instrument.
E1371.fix: Check the payment instruments enabled in CaaS configuration.

E1404.fix: Investigate with the externalTrxId and internalTrxId. Do not blind-retry.

E1405.description: Charging request timed out. No payments done.
E1405.fix: The subscriber did not confirm in time. Start a fresh charge only with a fresh, deliberate user action.

E1603.description: Temporary system error occurred while delivering your request.

E1604.fix: A URL the platform needs — such as the charging notification URL — is not configured on the application record.

E1607.fix: Your endpoint returned something the platform could not parse. Return HTTP 200 with {"statusCode":"S1000","statusDetail":"Success"}.

E1850.fix: Prompt the subscriber to re-enter it.

E1851.fix: Request a fresh OTP. mSpace does not publish the validity window.

E1852.description: Maximum number of OTP attempts has been reached.
E1852.fix: Stop accepting attempts against this reference and start a new OTP request.

E1853.description: Maximum number of OTP requests reached for this MSISDN or sender ID.
E1853.fix: Back off for this subscriber. Enforce your own per-number and per-IP rate limit as well.

E1855.fix: On CaaS, referenceNo must be the requestCorrelator returned by OTP generation; on the OTP API it must be the referenceNo returned by OTP Request.

E1856.description: Documented as "Invalid Request" on OTP Request, and as "OTP Not Found" on CaaS OTP verification and the charging notification.

E1857.description: Documented as "Internal Server Error Occur" on the OTP API, and as "Invalid Reference Number" on the charging notification.
E1857.fix: Retry only on the OTP API path. On a charging notification it is terminal — reconcile the transaction and do not re-charge.

E9999.description: System error, reported by CaaS OTP verification.

practices.title: Never hardcode applicationId or password
practices.detail: Environment variables only, through one config module, validated at startup. Not in source, not in a client bundle, not in a committed file, not in a log, not in git history. Never prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ / VITE_ / REACT_APP_.

practices.title: Never call mSpace from client-side code
practices.detail: Clients call your backend; your backend calls mSpace. The credentials are a shared secret and the platform enforces the Allowed Host Address list, which a mobile client cannot satisfy.

practices.title: Never subscribe or charge without recorded consent
practices.detail: Capture explicit consent with a timestamp and the channel before Subscription Register or any CaaS charge, and disclose the amount and frequency first. Both are configured per application in provisioning.

practices.title: Charging is idempotent on externalTrxId
practices.detail: Generate externalTrxId once per logical charge, persist it BEFORE the call, and reuse it unchanged on any resolution attempt. A retry with a fresh id can charge a real person twice.

practices.title: HTTP 200 does not mean success
practices.detail: mSpace returns HTTP 200 for application-level failures. Branch on statusCode. S1000 is success everywhere except CaaS OTP generation, where the documented success code is P1003, and Subscriber List, where S1001 means success with no matches.

practices.title: Treat subscriberId as opaque
practices.detail: With Mobile Number Masking enabled the platform sends a masked number rather than an MSISDN. Do not parse it, do not strip tel:, do not assume a length. Store it as given and send back exactly what you received.

practices.title: Guard tel:all
practices.detail: tel:all sends to the entire subscribed base. Put it in its own function behind an explicit confirmation and an authorisation check, and check the base size first.

practices.title: Acknowledge callbacks before doing work
practices.detail: Respond HTTP 200 with {"statusCode":"S1000","statusDetail":"Success"} immediately, then process out of band through the stack's real background mechanism. USSD sessions time out in seconds.

practices.title: Deduplicate every callback
practices.detail: Every callback can arrive more than once. Deduplicate on the documented key, and make a duplicate charging notification incapable of double-counting revenue.

practices.title: Never disable TLS verification
practices.detail: Disabling certificate validation exposes the applicationId and password that can charge your subscribers. If a chain is incomplete, supply the intermediate CA explicitly instead.

practices.title: Echo the USSD sessionId, and end with mt-fin
practices.detail: The USSD Gateway assigns the sessionId. Never generate one for a session the platform started, and close terminal screens with mt-fin or the session hangs until the network times it out.

practices.title: The USSD session store must be shared across instances
practices.detail: An in-process map works in development and breaks the moment a second instance or worker exists — a keypress routed elsewhere cannot see the session and the subscriber's menu dies mid-flow. Use Redis or equivalent, with a short TTL.

practices.title: Money is a decimal type
practices.detail: amount crosses the wire as a string. Hold it as BigDecimal, decimal.Decimal, decimal, bcmath or integer minor units in your own code — never a binary float.

practices.title: Set an explicit timeout on every call
practices.detail: No default-infinite requests. A timeout is a property of the protocol, so it belongs in the client as a constant rather than in configuration.

practices.title: Log identifiers, mask subscribers, never log secrets
practices.detail: Log requestId, sessionId, externalTrxId, internalTrxId and statusCode. Mask subscriberId. Never log the password, the OTP, referenceNo or requestCorrelator.

practices.title: Mirror subscription state locally
practices.detail: Consume the Subscription Notification URL and keep a local mirror rather than calling getStatus on every request. Subscriber List exists to catch up on notifications you missed.
